segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],
must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.
Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking
of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.

Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself.

'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does.

A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking.

'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side.

The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right.

Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. The presence of the device is the evidence of the permission and of its lawfulness, including the Department's determination for a highway it maintains (status reading): the words that limit where the authority may permit angle parking bind the authority, not the road user. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the permission of the place.

assumptions.meaning: the one-way way at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which the local authority having jurisdiction permits vehicles to park with their left-hand wheels at the left-hand curb, as the map's reading records

residues.why: The provisions the words point to are subsections (2) and (3), which are segments s7-s9 of this same text and are carried there as the exceptions of this node; the words add nothing beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is at rest at the observation (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); it occupies (rel.occupies) a highway region h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) some lane (st.lane) has a side whose marking type is curb (st.lane_marking); and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap.
obligation: At that observation, with h re-bound as in the applicability (a highway the subject occupies on which a lane has a curb-marked side), one of three holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (1) Right-hand curb: the subject occupies a travel region r lying on h whose designated direction d (st.lane_direction) has a dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge region e (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way) is on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset of e below zero) at a ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry) of at most 18 inches (literal). (2) Left-hand curb of a one-way highway, where asm.left_curb_parking_permitted holds: the subject occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on h with heading·d at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge e lying on h is on its left (offset above zero) within 18 inches of its body. (3) Angle parking permitted: the subject occupies a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or it occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.

narrowings.why: The wheels are not observed: the body outline stands for them. The wheels lie inside the footprint, so the body-to-curb distance is at most the wheel-to-curb distance and the reading is lenient by the wheels' inset (a few centimetres). 'parallel' is read within the tolerance p.parked_heading_cos, headed with the designated direction, since the right-hand wheels face the right-hand curb only so.

Why a vehicle is stopped is not observed. The words speak of a vehicle stopped or parked to stand by the way (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'); a halt made for traffic is read through the conduct that shows it: a halt in a region a signal, sign, railway device or person directing traffic governs, or a halt queued behind a member of traffic within the queue spacing. A halt mid-way through a parking manoeuvre is judged like any other halt.

The permission given by ordinance, and its validity on a highway the Department maintains, is read from the posted angle-parking sign or the angled bay marking: the presence of the device presumes the status.
The duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: Upon those highways which have official traffic-control devices permitting angle parking,
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle other than at the angle to the curb or edge of the highway indicated by such devices.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'permitting angle parking' is a regulatory sign of code 'angle_parking' (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), or a marked angle bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') the subject occupies whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's resolution. 'those highways' (st.highway) is read as the part of the way the device governs or marks, where the angle it indicates is defined. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read as the permission of the place.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion.

'stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that. 'other than at the angle ... indicated by such devices' maps to its nearest atoms: kin.heading, st.lane_direction, st.parking_space, st.road_edge (see the gap). The angle at which the vehicle meets the curb has as its cosine the dot product of its heading (kin.heading) with the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of the curb-side travel region; the angle the devices indicate is the bay's 'angle attribute' (st.parking_space), a number of degrees; the curb or edge is st.road_edge. No operator of the formula language relates a cosine to an angle given in degrees (Term has add, sub, mul, div, neg, abs and cond only), so whether the vehicle stands at the indicated angle cannot be written: see the operator gap.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.
obligation: Violated where the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance), its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region governed by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic, and no road user is ahead of it in its lane within p.queue_halt_gap between bodies), and it does not stand at the angle the device indicates: it occupies a parking space p of angle θ (st.parking_space) and the dot product of its heading (kin.heading) with the designated direction d (st.lane_direction) of the travel region on the same way nearest p differs from the cosine of θ by more than p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance. Where the subject is in a sign-governed region with no bay, the indicated angle is unobserved and the verdict of a non-traffic halt is unknown. The comparison of a cosine with θ needs the operator of the gap.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception (traffic conflict, a device's or an officer's direction) read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; standing's and parking's own exceptions (passengers, loading) are within that halting and add no further excuse.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

param_proposals.name: p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the largest difference between the cosine of the angle at which a standing vehicle meets the curb and the cosine of the angle a marked bay indicates at which the vehicle counts as standing at the bay's angle: about six degrees at a sixty-degree bay, the placement variability of a vehicle within a marked angle bay
param_proposals.source: angle-parking stall layout practice (stall angles of 30 to 90 degrees, with a few degrees of placement variability)

gaps.proposal: Term.cosDeg (a : Term) : the cosine of an angle a given in degrees, a ratio; unknown where a is unknown. It decides where the act is required: whether a vehicle stands at the angle the devices indicate, by comparing the cosine of its angle to the curb (the dot product of kin.heading with the curb-side carrier's st.lane_direction) with the cosine of the bay's angle (st.parking_space angle, deg).
gaps.nearest: kin.heading and st.lane_direction give the cosine of the vehicle's angle to the curb; st.parking_space gives the indicated angle in degrees; no Term relates the two (no trigonometric operator), and an approximation by a table of literal angles would be a model the words do not state.

segmentation.text: such lights shall be depressed or dimmed,
in the event cowl or parking lamps are not used.

elements.justification: 'lights are displayed' is a lamp of the vehicle lit: sig.headlamp 'state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}' not off, or sig.position_lamp 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit'. Neither is a stand-in for anything the contracts exclude; they are lamps lit.

'vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320 ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

Nearest atoms only: a posted parking prohibition (dev.regulatory_sign governing, dev.governs, the travel region the vehicle occupies) is one ground of unlawful parking among many; 'lawfully parked' is the verdict of every parking rule the vehicle's standing engages, which no atom carries and Formula.rule cannot compose, since the words name no rule. See the operator gap.

'parked' is DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading', which drv.motion.parked denotes: at rest at every observation of the window behind of length min_duration, a shorter halt being the temporary one the definition leaves out.
'nighttime' is env.darkness, 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter': the reading fixes the boundary, the atom carries the state.

'upon any highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is rel.occupies of st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; not the roadway alone.
'depressed or dimmed' is the headlamp beam lowered: sig.headlamp state low_beam (or off), never high_beam.

'cowl or parking lamps are not used' is the case in which the lights displayed are the headlamps rather than the cowl or parking lamps alone: sig.headlamp not off. sig.position_lamp cannot carry it: tail and position lamps are lit with the headlamps as well, so their being lit does not tell parking lamps used in place of headlamps.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, is parked (drv.motion.parked, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.parking_min_duration), occupies (rel.occupies) a highway (st.highway), in darkness (env.darkness), with a lamp lit (sig.headlamp not off, or sig.position_lamp), its headlamps being lit (sig.headlamp not off), and its parking is lawful (every parking rule it engages complied with: the operator of the gap).
obligation: The subject's headlamp state (sig.headlamp) is not high_beam.

gaps.proposal: Formula.compliesWithEngaged (who : Arg) (conduct : String) : at the observation, every rule of the set that governs conduct of the named kind (here standing or parking) and is engaged for road user who is complied with. It decides which road users the duty concerns: a vehicle lawfully parked, as against one parked against any parking rule (the same need as gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22 for 'in compliance with law').
gaps.nearest: dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region: a posted prohibition governing the vehicle's place is one ground of unlawful parking among many (distances from hydrants, crosswalks, curbs; durations), so its absence is not lawfulness; Formula.rule composes one named rule only, and the words name none.

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
except for the expeditious loading or unloading of goods.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'within' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... alley ...)'.

operationalizations.standard: expeditious loading or unloading of goods
operationalizations.convention: Loading or unloading is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains; 'expeditious' bounds how long that conduct may keep the vehicle standing. A halt counts as the expeditious loading or unloading the words except while the vehicle has not been at rest for longer than the temporary-halt bound of a loading zone (p.parking_min_duration): drv.motion.parked, at rest at every observation of that window behind, marks a halt beyond it.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district holds at its place; and asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold (where it holds the duty does not arise).
obligation: Violated where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration: at rest at every observation of the window behind, so beyond an expeditious halt for loading or unloading) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap. Compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; standing's and parking's own exceptions add no further excuse.
The purpose of the halt is not observed: any halt no longer than the temporary-halt bound is read as the excepted loading or unloading, and a longer one as not excepted, whatever the vehicle does.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
in such a manner, or under such conditions as to leave available less than 10 feet of the width of the alley for the free movement of vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing and parking are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are: drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap).

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; the vehicle in it is rel.occupies.

The width of the alley left available beside the halted vehicle is measured on each side from its body: to the alley's edge, a road edge region (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') on that side (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive)', read for its sign only) at the ground distance from the body (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); 'under such conditions' covers what else narrows that width beside it: an obstruction (st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user') on that side within the width, or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections ... share', at or above zero) on that side (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame') with a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral component) inside it. The width available is the free width on one side, never the two sides added, since a vehicle moves past on one side. 'the free movement of vehicular traffic' (traffic of vehicles, DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) names whom the width serves: the duty binds whether or not a vehicle is present to use it. The region distance is not a stand-in for occupancy; the bearing and overlap are not a contact or distance and are read only for side and alongside.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district does not hold at its place ('any other' alley: one not in a business district, the alleys of paragraph (a) being those in one); asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold; and its position leaves less than 10 feet (literal) of the alley's width free on either side: a side (left: prim.region_lateral_offset above zero, rel.bearing lateral component positive; right: below zero, negative) is free where some road edge region (st.road_edge) lies on that side, every road edge region on that side lies at a ground distance from the subject's body (st.region_geometry) of at least 10 feet, every obstruction (st.obstruction) on that side lies at least 10 feet from the body, and every other road user of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) on that side has a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral) of at least 10 feet; the condition holds where neither side is free.
obligation: The subject does not halt there: violated where it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap); compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
in such position as to block the driveway or entrance to any abutting property.

elements.justification: 'A person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing and parking are halts as well: drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap).

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'within' is rel.occupies.

Nearest atoms: blocking is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the mouth of the entrance, or its body standing across it within a gap (st.region_geometry); 'driveway' is DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner'. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' and is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's': inside an alley it would equally mark the alley's own junction with the street, which is no entrance to abutting property. See the atom gap.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley), and its position blocks the entrance to abutting property: its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the region where a driveway or other entrance to property meets the alley, or its body lies within p.entrance_block_gap of that region (st.region_geometry). Which regions are such entrances needs the atom of the gap.
obligation: The subject does not halt there: violated where it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap); compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

gaps.proposal: `st.property_entrance` | a driveway, private road or other entrance by which abutting property is entered from a highway or an alley, at the place where it meets that way **Not a stand-in for:** the junction of an alley or a public way with another way | general — it decides where a halt is forbidden: across the access to a property, as against at the alley's own mouth onto a street.
gaps.nearest: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's'; inside an alley it marks the alley's own junction as well as a property's driveway.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected prohibiting parking upon a narrow highway,

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'prohibiting parking upon a narrow highway' is the signed zone of kind narrow_highway (dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {..., narrow_highway, ...}'), whose legend's conditions hold at the observation (prim.conditions_hold; dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'), governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). The narrowness of the highway is the posting's designation, read from the sign (status), not a width the rule measures.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person parks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'park' is DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers', which drv.motion.parked denotes: at rest at every observation of the window behind of length min_duration, a shorter halt being the temporary one the definition leaves out (index: 'No person shall park' maps to drv.motion.parked).

'upon any such highway' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) of the highway the posting governs: the same region the trigger binds, the device's dev.governs relation fixing it.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) that a zone sign (dev.zone_sign) of kind narrow_highway governs (dev.governs), the sign's conditions holding at the observation for the subject (prim.conditions_hold).
obligation: The subject is not parked: violated where drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.parking_min_duration), compliant where it does not.

narrowings.why: Parking, a standing otherwise than temporarily for loading or unloading, is read through the halt's duration: a halt no longer than p.parking_min_duration is read as the temporary one.
The prohibition's legal status and the highway's designation as narrow are read from the posted narrow_highway zone sign.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected giving notice thereof,
shall not stand or park a vehicle
upon the left-hand side of a one-way

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'giving notice thereof', notice that standing or parking is prohibited there, are a regulatory sign of code no_standing or no_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold) governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), or a marked length of curb of kind no_parking or no_stopping (st.curb_zone, 'a signed or marked length of curb') the subject occupies. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the notice of the place.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stands or parks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'stand' is DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers', and every parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) is such a standing; the standing is drv.motion.parked with the passenger-dwell bound as its window, a shorter halt being read as the receiving or discharging of passengers the definition leaves out (index: 'No person shall stand or park a vehicle' maps to drv.motion.parked).

'a one-way' way is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction') lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway). Its 'left-hand side' is the side to the left of r's designated direction (st.lane_direction): a road edge (st.road_edge) on h is on that side where its lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'left positive', relative to the subject's heading) times the sign of the dot product of the subject's heading (kin.heading) with r's direction is positive. The subject stands upon the left-hand side where it lies nearer such a left edge than every right edge, by ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry). The offset is read only for its side; the distance is not a stand-in for occupancy.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, is in a place given notice of the prohibition: it occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code no_standing or no_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or a curb zone (st.curb_zone) of kind no_parking or no_stopping; it occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) inside an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city, 'street' being a highway inside the territorial limits of a city, DEF-NRS-484A-265); and it is on r's left-hand side: with s the sign of kin.heading · d for r's designated direction d (st.lane_direction), some road edge eL (st.road_edge) lying on h with s times its lateral offset (prim.region_lateral_offset) positive lies nearer the subject's body (st.region_geometry) than every road edge eR lying on h with s times its offset negative.
obligation: The subject is not standing: violated where drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.standing_min_duration), compliant where it does not.

narrowings.why: Standing, a halt otherwise than for receiving or discharging passengers, is read through the halt's duration: a halt no longer than the passenger-dwell bound p.standing_min_duration is read as the excepted one.
Notice of the prohibition is read from the posted no_standing or no_parking sign or the no_parking or no_stopping curb marking at the subject's place.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
